value.rationale: The classical SQS(16) is a canonical 3-(16,4,1) incidence design. Determining whether its signed four-point constraints lose information under arbitrary point-sign colorings is a natural recovery and coding-theoretic question, not an arbitrarily selected coordinate slice. Exact eight-level zero-free spectrum is structurally explained by quadratic-polar-rank, cubic-line, and quartic-point cases, and the precise 3617/840 inverse l1/linfty norm measures worst-case recovery amplification not specified by unsigned block counts or standard code-weight distributions. The finite exact domain and historical risks are stated.
